feature: A long edit plays, scrubs and edits without a stutter (pass 12)
summary: Clicking a clip when nothing is picked fills the right panel a piece at a time, and two pieces used to land in the same frame. Now one piece lands per frame, with a quiet frame after the heavy ones, so the longest catch while the 6 minute edit plays went from about 56 ms to about 31 (median of ten clicks; worst 89 to 63). A cut with nothing picked went from 89 to 53 ms at worst of three.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. The button on step 1 opens your own copy of the 6 minute reference edit in Photonz Dev; once made, File > Open reaches it too (Cmd-Shift-G, ~/Library/Caches/Photonz Reference Edit/Photonz Dev).

try.do: Open the 6 minute reference edit in Photonz Dev with the button below, then press Space to play the edit.
While it plays, click an empty part of the timeline so nothing is picked.
Click a clip on V1 and watch the picture while the panel fills in.
Click empty timeline again, then press B with the playhead over a clip.
Pick the clip again and open Effects to check the shadow's sliders are all there.

evaluate: Does the picture keep moving smoothly while the panel fills in after you click a clip?
Does the panel filling in top to bottom over about half a second read as fine, or as slow?
After a cut with nothing picked, does the cut piece's panel appear without the picture catching?
rough: Bars still not reached, so this task stays open. Short speed walk, worst of three: trim 20, blade 53 (was 89), undo 29, pick 33, trim picked 19, blade picked 51, undo picked 23, unpick 38, pick from nothing 70 (one sample a run, runs 70, 66, 31 and 55 in a fourth; over ten clicks in a walk of its own the median was 31 and the worst 63), against 16 ms. Scrub 2 frames behind (bar 1); 1 dropped frame a minute (bar 0).
The panel now takes about 13 per cent longer in all to fill in after a pick from nothing (about 440 ms against 390), in more, shorter frames.

Still long: the frame after the Appearance section lands, up to 55 ms, with nothing landing in it. That is SwiftUI working out focus and accessibility for every control Appearance brought; splitting Appearance into rows that arrive a frame apart, as Effects does, is the next lead.
Tried and not kept: the panel in a drawing host of its own (a tenth off the total, no single frame shorter) and keeping each panel row's narrowest width between layouts (no change you could measure).
No mock covers this. It is speed work, and nothing on screen changed.
